thesis: BILL signed a definitive agreement on 2026-11-19 (8-K filed) to be taken private by TPG with Corpay at $63.25 per share in cash (~$6.0B). With the stock at $61.45 the remaining upside is capped at roughly the deal spread, while the downside if the deal fails to close is a return toward pre-rumor levels; the 14x volume spike reflects deal-related repositioning rather than a new operating signal. This suggests the risk/reward for a new short-term long entry is unattractive. A competing higher bid (Hellman & Friedman held talks earlier in 2026) is the main counter-case, but nothing found indicates an active rival bid, and the stock already trades below the agreed price.
invalidation: A competing higher bid emerges or the agreement is terminated/renegotiated

thesis: SK hynix ADRs are down ~37% over 60 calendar days and sit within 0.2% of their post-listing low after today's broad semiconductor selloff (Nasdaq-wide AI/chip rout tied to an SEC probe of Nvidia and short-seller claims on AMD). Company-specific overhangs include held-up U.S. export licenses for its China NAND plants and a U.S. DRAM price-fixing class action that survived a motion to dismiss in mid-November (no scheduled next ruling date found). The decline is largely sector- and sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed deterioration in SK hynix's own results, which suggests no clear entry signal while the memory complex is being de-rated. A 2005 guilty plea in a prior DRAM price-fixing case is outside the 3-year governance window.
invalidation: Memory/semiconductor selloff stabilizes and SKHY reclaims prior support (~$120) on company-specific positive news

thesis: Brookfield Infrastructure completed its corporate simplification on 2026-11-19: BIP and BIPC were combined into Brookfield Infrastructure Partners Inc., BIPC holders receive BIP Inc. Class A shares one-for-one, and the new shares are expected to trade as 'BIP' on the NYSE from 2026-11-23 (BIPC ticker going away). Today's 5x volume spike and the recent run-up look largely mechanical, driven by the share conversion and related index/holder repositioning rather than a disclosed fundamental change. This suggests no actionable entry in the BIPC line itself; any interest should be re-screened under the new BIP ticker.
invalidation: Not applicable to BIPC after conversion; re-evaluate under ticker BIP once it trades

thesis: P&G is up ~15% over 60 calendar days and trades within 2.4% of its 52-week high. At its 2026-11-19 Investor Day it set a target of up to $10B in productivity savings through FY2030 (including a 20-30% cut to the supply-chain workforce) and maintained its FY27 outlook (core EPS $6.89-$7.11), which includes ~$1B of after-tax cost pressure. The rally also coincides with a broad rotation into defensive staples as tech sells off. The picture is mixed: the savings plan is a real company-specific positive, but analysts questioned how much is new versus offsetting cost inflation, profit guidance is close to flat, and consensus targets (~$175) leave little upside. The consolidated 'Protect, Grow, Restore' greenwashing MDL has a pending motion to dismiss but no scheduled ruling date found.
invalidation: Close back below ~$160 or FY27 core EPS guidance cut

thesis: Home Depot reported fiscal Q3 2026 on 2026-11-17: sales $43.4B (+4.9%), comps +2.2%, adjusted EPS +3.2% to $3.86, and it narrowed full-year guidance to ~4.5% sales growth, ~1.4% comps and ~2% adjusted EPS growth. The stock is up ~13% over 60 calendar days. The confirmed results show DIY/small-project demand holding up, but the operating-margin outlook sits at the low end of the prior range and the housing market is still slumping, so several factors pull in different directions without one clearly dominant. The release also refers to an incoming CEO (Richard McPhail); nothing found ties this to execution problems, so it reads as planned succession, but it was not independently confirmed. No litigation with a scheduled near-term ruling or governance event was found.
invalidation: Next quarter's comps turn negative or FY guidance is cut

thesis: Costco reported October 2026 net sales of $24.50B (+12.6%) with total comps +11.1% and U.S. comps +12.6% (company release, 2026-11-04), and the stock is up ~22% over 60 calendar days to within 1.8% of its 52-week high, closing higher today despite the broad market selloff. The strongest counter-evidence is that gasoline price inflation contributed a meaningful part of the comp, the stock trades at ~53x earnings, and consumers have filed proposed class actions over tariff-refund pass-through; even so, comps remain strong ex-gas, the class actions face pending motions to dismiss with no scheduled ruling found, and Costco disclosed receiving $184M of IEEPA tariff refunds that it says will fund member price cuts. This suggests the confirmed sales momentum still supports holding.
invalidation: Monthly comps ex-gas decelerate sharply or Q1 FY27 membership-fee/renewal metrics weaken

thesis: Lilly reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-29 with revenue +39% to $24.4B on Mounjaro/Zepbound and raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91-92B (non-GAAP EPS $35-36). The stock is up ~16% over 60 calendar days and sits ~8.7% below its 2026-11-16 52-week high after easing with the market this week. Counterweights include an FDA request for additional safety data on oral obesity drug Foundayo (orforglipron) and pending pricing litigation (Pennsylvania insulin suit filed 2026-10-20; Strive antitrust suit), none with a scheduled ruling found in the next ~90 days. The confirmed earnings and guidance raise suggest the holding remains supported, though the Foundayo safety-data question isn't fully resolved.
invalidation: Guidance cut, material Foundayo label/safety setback, or GLP-1 pricing action that hits tirzepatide revenue

thesis: Linde is up ~11.5% over 60 calendar days and remains above its 200-day average, but its Q3 2026 results were mixed: sales rose 9% to $9.4B (underlying +5%) while net income and diluted EPS fell ~12% and ~11% year over year. Trefis attributes the stock's flat stretch since mid-2026 mainly to higher interest rates weighing on valuations. A quarterly $1.60 dividend is declared (record 2026-12-03). With offsetting top-line growth and earnings decline and no fresh company-specific catalyst found, the evidence is mixed rather than a clear net read; it still suggests holding rather than exiting, since no deterioration beyond the reported EPS decline was found. No litigation with a scheduled ruling or governance event was found.
invalidation: Close below the 200-day average or a further guidance reduction

thesis: Visa reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-10-27: net revenue ~$12.1B (+13%) and non-GAAP EPS $3.48 (+17%), with FY27 guidance for low-double-digit revenue growth and low-double-digit to low-teens EPS growth. The stock is ~9% below its 2026-11-05 52-week high, roughly flat on the day amid today's broad selloff. The DOJ debit-monopolization suit (SDNY) remains open with no scheduled ruling or trial date found in the next ~90 days, and Visa has continued settling merchant interchange claims. This suggests the fundamentals still support holding, though the pullback from the high and the unresolved DOJ case keep this short of a clean read.
invalidation: Payment-volume growth slows materially or an adverse ruling/schedule in the DOJ debit case

thesis: Apple trades ~5% below its 2026-11-13 52-week high and well above its 200-day average; today's ~1.9% decline came with the broad tech selloff rather than company news. No fresh company-specific catalyst was found this run. The planned CEO transition to John Ternus (effective 2026-09-01) was routine succession, not tied to execution problems. The DOJ iPhone antitrust case is in discovery with fact discovery running into 2027 and no trial date set. With the recent move driven by sector-wide sentiment and no new company-disclosed catalyst, this suggests continuing to hold, but without a strong signal.
invalidation: Close below the 200-day average or a company-specific negative (guidance cut, adverse antitrust ruling)
